searchText: things got worse on devnet-4. we have a massive forking party on the previous canonical chain after we bumped the blob count :/ we've lowered the blob spamming again - hoping clients agree on the 2 major chains again. Something to keep in mind for all clients: our Victoriametrics (prometheus) cluster was overwhelmed today from the devnet-4 load. The largest contributor was supernodes that have libp2p metrics based on `topic`. With BPO's every 24h on this devnet each client was generating a fresh set of libp2p metrics with every BPO. It might make sense for clients to reset those metrics at the fork epoch? I imagine we'd see this with some users on mainnet if we queue up 3 BPO's at a time too Hi, Sunnyside Labs published a fusaka-devnet-3 spec devnet report that was tested before devnet-4. We believe it can help predict fusaka-devnet-4 behavior once current issues are resolved and high-blob-load testing resumes. We hit 72 blobs/block peaks and sustained >60 blobs (10-min avg) under 60 M gas, a 1-in-4 supernode ratio, and bandwidth caps. Instability appeared when full-node uplink (~25 Mbps) saturated, causing slower propagation, more attestation disagreement, and reorgs. GetBlobsV2 performance under heavy load varied by ELs. Please find the report: https://www.notion.so/testinprod/Sunnyside-Devnet-Updates-08-13-24e8fc57f54680088514eccdca62c560?source=copy_link On devnet-4, are CL bootnodes healthy? I am not able to find any correct peer if using the provided list of bootnodes. However, If I add this ENR to the list: ``` - enr:-Ni4QBl06VXhyrctr9Wii_yZSfgSl5gyKqLoFOB6BK46DSw3d5Efc8wBVtHkioLXMd5eqvO0Ey9zxNOTEF07FSxlSoyGAZiFyfaqh2F0dG5ldHOIAADAAAAAAACDY2djCIRldGgykAsb3OhwEDgTAAUAAAAAAACCaWSCdjSCaXCEj_SAwoNuZmSEWJxiGoRxdWljgjLIiXNlY3AyNTZrMaEDIUQM0ecJBJt-jRX3Aj-E5DiQecReaXwL1Vw5hqegnV2Ic3luY25ldHMAg3RjcIIjKIN1ZHCCIyg ``` (which is `prysm-nethermind-full-1`) then I am able to sync. They're all using geth, and I'm resyncing the geth nodes with potential fixes. So likely they're down. Thanks! (But no pressure at all, adding other nodes to the local bootnodes list is a good enough workaround)

excerpts.content:
things got worse on devnet-4. we have a massive forking party on the previous canonical chain after we bumped the blob count :/
we've lowered the blob spamming again - hoping clients agree on the 2 major chains again.

excerpts.author: samcm
excerpts.content:
Something to keep in mind for all clients: our Victoriametrics (prometheus) cluster was overwhelmed today from the devnet-4 load. The largest contributor was supernodes that have libp2p metrics based on `topic`. 

With BPO's every 24h on this devnet each client was generating a fresh set of libp2p metrics with every BPO. It might make sense for clients to reset those metrics at the fork epoch? I imagine we'd see this with some users on mainnet if we queue up 3 BPO's at a time too

excerpts.author: sunnysidedj_42398
excerpts.content: Hi, Sunnyside Labs published a fusaka-devnet-3 spec devnet report that was tested before devnet-4. We believe it can help predict fusaka-devnet-4 behavior once current issues are resolved and high-blob-load testing resumes. We hit 72 blobs/block peaks and sustained >60 blobs (10-min avg) under 60 M gas, a 1-in-4 supernode ratio, and bandwidth caps. Instability appeared when full-node uplink (~25 Mbps) saturated, causing slower propagation, more attestation disagreement, and reorgs. GetBlobsV2 performance under heavy load varied by ELs. Please find the report: https://www.notion.so/testinprod/Sunnyside-Devnet-Updates-08-13-24e8fc57f54680088514eccdca62c560?source=copy_link
